Large Linear Systems 2: General Systems and Exponentials¶

Not every system is symmetric, and not every linear problem asks for a solve: sometimes you want the matrix exponential applied to a vector. This chapter covers restarted GMRES for general systems and the Arnoldi evaluation of exp(t A) v. After it you can solve non-symmetric systems matrix-free, tune the restart, and advance a linear evolution without forming a dense exponential.

Every program is complete and its output is the output of that program.

GMRES for general systems¶

krylov::GmresResult krylov::gmres(apply, rhs, solve_dims, GmresOptions options = {}, initial = undefined);

GMRES builds an orthonormal basis of the Krylov space, finds the combination that minimises the residual, and restarts from the result. It works for any invertible real or complex operator.

GmresOptions

Meaning

Default

max_iterations

total iteration cap

128

restart

basis size before restarting

24

relative_tolerance, absolute_tolerance

stopping tolerances

1e-8, 1e-10

rank_tolerance

numerical-rank threshold used when the basis degenerates

1e-12

GmresResult has solution, residual_norm, relative_residual, per-lane converged, iterations, operator_evaluations and restarts.

  • The restart length

The action of a matrix exponential¶

krylov::ExpResult krylov::exp_action(apply, v, solve_dims, double time, ExpOptions options = {});

This computes exp(time · A) v by an Arnoldi projection. It is the solution at time time of y' = A y starting from v, and it is how large linear evolutions (diffusion, wave and Schrödinger equations on a grid) are advanced exactly in time, with no time-stepping error.

ExpOptions

Meaning

Default

max_iterations

size of the Krylov space

32

relative_tolerance, absolute_tolerance

accuracy for the residual estimate

1e-9, 1e-12

ExpResult has value, residual_estimate (the standard a-posteriori Krylov estimate), per-lane converged, iterations and operator_evaluations.

  • Heat flow

Checklist¶

  1. Not symmetric: gmres. Count operator_evaluations, and try several restart lengths.

  2. Linear evolution y' = A y: exp_action, growing max_iterations until converged.

  3. gmres and exp_action accept complex operators and vectors; cg and pcg are for real systems.

  4. Use the residual estimate and the converged flags; they are the stopping evidence.
